data.one_liner: Unified API for native key-value storage across platforms
data.what_it_does: Provides a simple interface for reading and writing key-value pairs to platform-native storage such as iOS Keychain, Android SharedPreferences, and Windows Registry. It supports synchronous, asynchronous (via isolates), and secure encrypted storage.
use_when: Storing non-sensitive data that should persist across app restarts
Storing sensitive data that needs encryption and isolation from the UI thread
Need a single API that works on Android, iOS, macOS, Linux, Windows, and Web
Migrating from platform-specific storage solutions to a unified API
avoid_when: Using secure storage on Web, as it is only in-memory and not persistent
Requiring secure storage on Android versions below API 29
When you need advanced database features like SQL or NoSQL
strengths: Cross-platform support with a single API
Built-in secure encryption for sensitive data
Asynchronous APIs via isolates to avoid UI blocking
Supports both local and secure storage variations
weaknesses: Web secure storage is in-memory and not persistent
Requires native setup for secure storage on Android (min API 29)

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: Simple key-value storage without secure encryption, lighter weight

alternatives.name: flutter_secure_storage
alternatives.why_pick_it: Provides secure storage with platform-specific implementations, but lacks unified API across all platforms
